citations.title: Earning Power: Project Management Salary Survey, 13th Edition
citations.what_it_says: PMP-certified project managers report ~16% higher median salary in the US than non-certified peers, with median US compensation around $123,000.

citations.title: Pulse of the Profession 2023: Power Skills, Redefining Project Success
citations.what_it_says: Organizations report higher project success rates when PMs hold formal credentials such as PMP, and demand for credentialed PMs is rising in healthcare and IT sectors.

citations.title: 2023 HIMSS Healthcare Workforce Survey
citations.what_it_says: Healthcare IT employers cite project management certification among the most-requested non-clinical credentials for implementation and digital-transformation roles.

citations.authors: Gemunden HG, Lehner P, Kock A
citations.title: Project management in healthcare: A systematic literature review
citations.what_it_says: Formal PM methodology adoption (including PMP-aligned PMBOK practice) is associated with improved healthcare implementation outcomes and is a growing competency expectation for healthcare PMs.

citations.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook: Project Management Specialists
citations.what_it_says: Project management specialists earn a median annual wage of ~$98,580 with faster-than-average projected growth, and PMP is the most commonly cited preferred credential.

citations.title: Competencies for the clinical informatics workforce: an analysis of job postings
citations.journal: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
citations.what_it_says: Analysis of clinical informatics and health IT job postings shows project management certification (PMP) appears as a preferred qualification in a significant share of senior implementation and consulting roles.
